newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil rally continues.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil rally continues.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swap rally continued late afternoon in the wake of tight prompt supplies and steady buying interest from both traders and Chinese consumers, market sources said on Thursday.
December gas oil swaps was last quoted at $31.55/$31.70, up about 20 cents from the midday level of $31.30.$31.45, brokers said.
Traders said the rise was due to expected further buying interest from traders for physical cargoes with most sellers said sold out for December product in Singapore.
"There was active trading for January swaps but no deals were seen for December," one broker said.
January traded earlier today at $31.45, $31.53 and $31.59 a barrel, one broker said. The December/January backwardation remained at a steep $1.00 value.

Traders said December swaps were expected to remain firm as there were no alternative supply source but January may come under some pressure as the arbitrage for exports from the west is slowly becoming viable.
The east-west spread is currently at about $10.00 per tonne in favour of the east and if this spread widens further by about $2-3 the arbitrage would open, traders said.

The jet fuel/gas oil spread (regrade) came under strong selling pressure late afternoon on reports of reduced buying from North Asia for January. December and January regrade were offered at $1.60, down 30 cents from earlier today.
December jet fuel swap was offered at $32.90 a barrel down about 50 cents from its traded level of $33.40 earlier this week, brokers said.
With lack of firm direction from crude, December naphtha was unchanged at $23.60/$23.85 and fuel oil at $118.75/$119.50.
